jobs.description: Copenhagen, Denmark Join Saxo’s First Line of Defence as a Senior Regulatory Specialist Are you passionate about navigating complex regulatory landscapes and transforming regulatory requirements into practical business solutions? Do you thrive in a dynamic environment where regulation, strategy, and business operations intersect? The job At Saxo, we are looking for an experienced Senior Regulatory Specialist to play a key role in our First Line of Defence. You will act as a trusted advisor to the business, ensuring strong regulatory oversight, driving regulatory change initiatives, and fostering constructive relationships with supervisory authorities across multiple jurisdictions. This is an opportunity to make a tangible impact in a global, technology-driven financial institution where pragmatic, risk-based compliance enables innovation and growth. As our Senior Regulatory Specialist, you will: Own and enhance key regulatory processes and reporting activities, ensuring accuracy, quality, and timely delivery. Act as the primary point of contact for supervisory authorities, leading proactive engagement and coordinating responses to regulatory inquiries. Interpret regulatory requirements and translate them into practical controls, policies, and operating procedures that support business objectives. Lead cross-functional implementation of new regulations, products, and jurisdictional requirements across the organisation. Partner with local offices and stakeholders globally to strengthen and harmonise regulatory capabilities. Oversee third-party providers supporting regulatory obligations and ensure effective delivery and governance. Identify opportunities for process improvements and contribute to the continuous enhancement of the regulatory framework. Your profile To succeed in this role, you will have: A minimum of 8 years of regulatory experience within financial services, gained in a first, second, or third line function. Demonstrated experience leading regulatory change initiatives and resolving complex regulatory issues from assessment through implementation. Strong analytical capabilities, control design expertise, and an ability to work confidently with data. A pragmatic, solution-oriented mindset with a focus on risk management and continuous improvement. Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to influence across functions, cultures, and seniority levels. Fluency in English, both written and spoken; Danish is considered an advantage. Join a fast-growing international MedTech company and take a central role in turning AI ambitions into practical, adopted solutions across the organisation.

Turn AI ambitions into practical business impact

Contura International has been named a Gazelle company two years in a row and has experienced significant growth over the past five years, increasing revenue fivefold and its number of employees tenfold.

As AI Lead, you will join Contura's IT & Projects organisation and report to the Head of IT.

In this newly established role, you will take ownership of the AI roadmap and use-case portfolio and help move AI initiatives from pilot to production.

Working across business and IT, you will drive adoption, build internal AI capability and ensure that initiatives create business value while meeting relevant quality and compliance requirements.

Your key responsibilities include:

• Own and drive Contura's AI roadmap, use-case portfolio and implementation plan.

• Translate business needs into qualified use cases, requirements and solution proposals.

• Take successful AI and digital solutions from pilot into controlled production.

• Build internal AI capability through training, workshops and an AI community of champions and key users.

• Coordinate external specialists and contribute to pragmatic AI governance together with IT, Quality and Regulatory Affairs.

Business-minded AI profile with strong implementation skills

We are open regarding your professional background and previous job title. What matters most is your ability to understand business needs, turn them into relevant AI or digital solutions and create momentum from idea through implementation and adoption.

We imagine that you bring:

• Experience taking AI or digital solutions from pilot to production and driving user adoption.

• Experience translating business needs into solution proposals, requirements and priorities.

• Practical understanding of data foundations, data quality and integrations.

• Experience with AI and data solutions, preferably within the Microsoft ecosystem.

• Strong communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to make AI understandable and relevant across the business.

You are pragmatic, curious and delivery-oriented and comfortable creating structure and direction in an area that is still developing. You work well across functions and combine a strategic perspective with practical execution and a clear focus on business outcomes.

Turn AI into lasting business capability

This is an opportunity to take a central role in how Contura develops and applies AI as the company continues its growth and digitalisation journey.

About the job Our purpose is to bring hope to life by enabling life-changing therapies for patients around the globe, creating a healthier and happier tomorrow. Our mission is to work side by side with our customers to improve patients’ lives by bringing new biopharmaceuticals to market. Are you a detail-oriented student who thrives on organizing information and supporting technical teams? Do you want hands-on experience in a fast-paced biopharmaceutical environment? Then join AGC Biologics as a Student Assistant in our Equipment Maintenance and Calibration team—where your work helps map and optimize our cutting-edge production facilities. At AGC Biologics, you’ll join a fast-growing biopharmaceutical company where quality, collaboration, and continuous improvement are part of everyday life. As Student Assistant in our Equipment Maintenance and Calibration team, you’ll play a key role in organizing information, analysing data, mapping our facilities, and supporting the team while they keep our production and utility systems running at top performance—supporting life-changing treatments for patients worldwide. About the Team The Equipment Maintenance and Calibration team in Engineering comprises of dedicated technicians, engineers, and coordinators with a strong focus on personal development, collaboration, and high professional standards. We operate with a flat structure where every contribution matters and decisions are made collaboratively. Our culture emphasizes ownership, continuous learning, and mutual support. We work closely together to maintain critical production equipment and promote a safe, innovative, and engaging work environment. About the Role As a Student Assistant in our Equipment Maintenance and Calibration team, you will be primarily responsible for: Support the day-to-day operations of the Equipment Maintenance and Calibration team (e.g., data entry, document control, coordinating small tasks) Lead the facility mapping initiative by collecting and verifying the Process and Instrumentation Drawings (PIDs), building layouts, electrical and utility drawings, service and maintenance agreements, and spare-parts inventories, etc. Consolidate information into our CMMS or a central digital repository, ensuring accuracy and ease of access for the team Assist in updating and maintaining equipment records, location tags, and asset lists Collaborate with technicians and engineers to clarify technical details and resolve gaps in documentation Contribute ideas for improving our documentation processes and data workflows Analyze facility data (drawings, service agreements, spare-parts inventories, etc.) to identify gaps, validate completeness and produce clear, data-driven reports that guide maintenance planning and process improvements. This role offers flexible hours to accommodate your study schedule and the possibility of a longer-term internship if desired. Your Qualifications We are looking for a candidate who: Is enrolled in a relevant technical or engineering program (e.g., mechanical, electrical, industrial engineering, etc.), preferably in the first year of your education Demonstrates strong organizational skills and a keen eye for detail Has excellent communication skills in English and preferably Danish, both written and verbal Is proficient with Microsoft Office (Excel, Visio, Power BI) and eager to learn CMMS tools or CAD basics Is self-motivated, reliable, and able to work independently as well as part of a team What We Offer This role will give you insight into the design and operation of biopharmaceutical production facilities, as well as how the various departments collaborate to deliver life-changing therapies. On top of that, we offer the following: Meaningful tasks that directly support our maintenance operations and facility improvements Mentoring from experienced technicians and engineers Flexible scheduling to balance work and studies A collaborative, supportive work culture in a leading biopharmaceutical company How to Apply Applications are screened on an ongoing basis. If this sounds like the right challenge for you, we’d love to hear from you. Don’t hesitate to apply – even if you don’t meet every single requirement. The right mindset matters just as much. If we see a potential match, one of our recruiters will contact you to discuss your application. If you have any questions, please contact Sameer Ahmed (Senior Manager, Equipment Maintenance and Calibration) on +45 50106391 or on LinkedIn. From our Søborg site, we develop and manufacture life‑changing advanced biologics for some of the world’s most innovative pharmaceutical companies. Together with our team members across Europe, the U.S., and Japan, we deliver development and manufacturing of mammalian and microbial-based therapeutic proteins, plasmid DNA (pDNA), messenger RNA (mRNA), viral vectors, and genetically engineered cells therapies. Across our global network, we are united by one mission: To work side by side with our customers in order to improve patients’ lives by bringing new biopharmaceuticals to market. AGC Biologics is Your Friendly CDMO Expert – dedicated partners with the expertise and commitment to support our customers and teams. Are you passionate about delivering great customer experiences and solving technical challenges?

At Trackman, we are looking for a service-minded and technically curious Customer Service Specialist to join our Business Tools Support team.

In this role, you will be a key point of contact for customers worldwide, helping them get the most out of our innovative sports technology. From troubleshooting technical issues to guiding new customers through onboarding, you will play an important role in delivering a seamless and professional customer experience.

You will join an international and collaborative environment where customer satisfaction, problem-solving, and continuous improvement are at the heart of what we do.

Meet the Team

You will join our Business Tools Support team in EMEA, a collaborative team of six supporting the digital platforms and services used by Trackman venues worldwide, including Booking & Payments, the Trackman Portal, and venue onboarding.

Working closely with customers, Sales, Product, and Development, the team resolves technical and operational challenges and continuously improves our solutions. You will have the opportunity to develop your technical knowledge, support international customers, and contribute to delivering excellent customer experiences.

What will you be doing?

As a Customer Service Specialist, you will combine customer service with hands-on technical support. Your key responsibilities will include:

• 
Customer Support: Respond to customer inquiries via phone and email, providing professional, friendly, and efficient assistance.

• 
Technical Troubleshooting: Identify, diagnose, and resolve technical issues related to Trackman products, software, and connected devices.

• 
Customer Onboarding: Guide new customers through product setup, configuration, and usage, ensuring they feel confident using our solutions.

• 
Product Guidance: Educate customers on product features, updates, and best practices to help them get the most out of Trackman technology.

• 
Case Management: Handle multiple support requests, prioritize effectively, and maintain accurate documentation in our support system.

• 
Follow-up & Customer Satisfaction: Proactively follow up on customer cases to ensure successful resolutions and positive experiences.

• 
Collaboration & Improvement: Work closely with colleagues and other departments to resolve complex issues, share knowledge, and continuously improve our support processes.

What are we looking for?

We are looking for someone who enjoys helping people, has a natural interest in technology, and thrives in a dynamic, international environment.

Ideally, you bring:

• 
Previous experience in customer service, technical support, or a similar customer-facing role, preferably within a technology-related industry.

• 
Strong communication skills in English, both written and spoken.

• 
A customer-focused mindset with excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting abilities.

• 
Confidence working with Windows operating systems, computers, and common technical devices such as monitors, projectors, and mobile devices.

• 
Experience with ticketing or customer support systems, preferably Zendesk.

• 
The ability to manage multiple requests, prioritize tasks, and maintain a high level of service in a busy environment.

• 
A proactive, structured, and collaborative approach to your work.

It would be an advantage if you also have:

• 
An interest in sports, particularly golf, baseball, or sports technology.

• 
Basic knowledge of networking and connectivity.

• 
Experience with remote troubleshooting and technical diagnostics.

• 
Additional education or training in IT, customer service, or a related field.

• 
Flexibility to work weekends when required.

Most importantly, you are curious, eager to learn, and motivated by making a difference for customers.

What can we offer?

At Trackman, you will become part of an international technology company where innovation, sports, and passion come together.

You will have the opportunity to work with advanced sports technology used by athletes, coaches, and organizations worldwide, alongside talented and dedicated colleagues.

We offer a collaborative working environment, opportunities to develop your technical and customer service skills, and a culture where initiative, ownership, and new ideas are valued.

The Office

We are located at DTU Science Park in Hørsholm. We take great pride in the state-of-art building we have designed! The office features bright meeting rooms, coffee areas to catch up with colleagues, a large testing arena with simulators available for employees and a fitness center, everything surrounded by a beautiful forest and respecting the environment. We made sure to utilize the newest technologies to be energy efficient and be mindful of ventilation and sound propagation. The cherry on top is our canteen: with an indoor and outdoor area to enjoy the fresh food prepared by our own kitchen staff.

Join the home of a powerful sports brand and a one-of-a-kind technology

Our proprietary technology is based on expert knowledge about radar, computer vision, data, and software engineering. Our solutions are developed by specialists who endlessly explore and challenge new technical boundaries. Trackman’s blend of cutting-edge technology, sports, and continued growth make our company an outstanding place to work.

Our work culture is entrepreneurial, ambitious, and rewarding as you get to collaborate with inspiring colleagues and interact with the leaders of golf, baseball, and football. Based on a unique brand reputation, we are proud to work in close partnership with the top athletes, organizations, and teams that rely on our technology to stay ahead of the race.

We are a Danish company founded, owned, and managed since 2003 by three entrepreneurs with a strong passion for sports. Today, we have a global footprint with our headquarters located in Denmark (Hørsholm) and offices in New York, Phoenix, Seoul and Tokyo. We employ over 1000+ people worldwide, half of which work in Denmark, where most hardware and software products are developed, tested, and manufactured.

Where innovation happens

At Trackman, we know that great people make great products. We believe that teams thrive, and innovation sparks in an atmosphere where people are encouraged to think for themselves, where everybody’s voices are heard, and where the best ideas prevail in the pursuit of exceptional solutions. This mix makes Trackman an inspiring company – for our customers and colleagues.

Share our Passion!

If you are excited about combining technology, customer service, and sports, we would love to hear from you!

For additional information about the position, please contact Jade Palphreyman, Business Tools Lead EMEA, at japa@trackman.com.

**The Role

**The Senior Manager, Biostatistics acts as a biostatistician supporting the clinical development of compounds as compound lead, primarily up until proof of concept, and/or as trial responsible statistician.

**Responsibilities

**Compound/Indication Level

• Act as lead and main point of contact related to Statistics for designated compound/indication

• Follow scientific and technical progress within the field of biostatistics in drug development and advise of new methodologies that may support innovation and improve efficiencies

• Engage with regulatory authorities on compound/indication level discussions

• Acts as a role model

• Ensures consistency of statistical methods and data handling across trials

• Ensures all compound/indication related work and information is shared between biostatisticians involved in the compound and with the vendor

• Supports compound responsible programmer in developing an integrated database specification

**CDT Member

**

• Responsible for giving statistical input to overall strategy and the synopsis development in the CDT

• Provide scientific advice to the CDT including design of trials, analyses and analyses requiring advanced statistical methodologies/techniques

• Represent the CDT/the company at regulatory meetings, during Key Opinion Leaders meetings, network and/or Partner meetings, as applicable

• Drive design and synopsis development together with relevant stakeholders

• Ensure transparent communication to relevant stakeholders from the CDT

• Ensure availability of integrated database(s), as needed, and planning and conduct of integrated analysis to support development decisions, submissions, and marketing needs

• Support development and communication in relation to communication strategy and/or scientific input to presentations, posters, and articles

Trial Level

• Represent Genmab during meetings/congresses and courses and perform professional networking

• Engage with regulatory authorities on trial level discussions

• Arranges/attends lessons learned to share learnings

• Represents Genmab during Key Opinion Leaders meetings

• Ensure biostatistician review of partner synopsis, protocols, statistical analysis plans, results meetings presentations and clinical trial reports

• Coordinate data transfers from/to business partners in collaboration with the programmer and the data manager, as applicable

**CTT Member

**

• Participate and represent Biostatistics

• Review and provide input to protocol and amendment development

• Perform vendor oversight according to applicable SOPs

• Give input to eCRF setup, edit checks, validation plan, protocol deviations classifications, DSUR, IB updates, tables, figures, and listings etc.

• Review assay validation reports, as applicable

• Perform exploratory analysis, ad hoc analyses, and modelling of data

• Review and approve randomization and stratification plans

• Perform UAT of Randomization part of the IRT system as applicable

• Ensure procedures for blinding are in place as applicable

• Support timely delivery of statistical deliverables

• Responsible for planning and conducting trial result meetings

• Review and approve the CSR

• Attend operational and steering committee meetings, as applicable

• Support regulatory submission/filing activities

**Requirements

**

• MS / PhD or equivalent in a statistical discipline

• 5+ years of experience in relevant area preferred or demonstrated capability

• Experience in statistical analysis, modelling and simulation and adaptive trial designs

• Experience in working with clinical trials

• Preferred experience with oncology clinical trials

• Proficient programming skills in statistical software’s, such as SAS

• Excellent oral and written communication skills

• Ability to work independently as well as in teams

• Confident, self-reliant, and a quick learner

• Proactive and open-minded

• Ability to prioritize and work in a fast-paced and changing environment

• Result and goal-oriented and committed to contributing to the overall success of Genmab

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Job Description

This role is based in Taastrup, Denmark, and requires strong on-site presence in the data center environment. We are only open to applicants already based in Denmark

Are you an expert in ensuring uptime and high quality in a Data Center, or would you like to become one? Then here is a unique opportunity to oversee the operation and maintenance of multiple data centers!

If you have the following, this job is for you:

• Technical education: It can be as a marine engineer, electrician, refrigeration technician, energy technologist, automation technologist or similar

• Relevant experience with Critical Facilities: e.g., Electrical, mechanical, generators, automation, HVAC, buildings automation etc.

• Practical experience with troubleshooting and servicing technical installations

• Experience from operations in a technical environment - preferably data centers

• Meeting customer and government security screening requirements are required for this role

About the role and the team

GlobalConnect operates 11 data centers in Denmark and even more in the other countries where GlobalConnect is present. In addition to the ongoing operation and maintenance of our existing Data centers, there are also large expansions in the pipeline. As our new Data Center Critical Facilities Engineer, you will be part of the Site Operations department with over 45 skilled team members, with colleagues in Norway, Finland, Sweden, Denmark and Germany and with employees from many nationalities, enabling you to work in a multinational environment.

Site Operations Denmark is a workplace with focus on a good working environment. We focus on professional and personal well-being and emphasize good working relationships. Through your work as a Critical Facilities, you will have the chance to engage with every facet of managing a data center. You will experience flexibility in relation to your everyday life and a large degree of freedom under responsibility. You can also expect that most days you will be met with exciting projects and tasks that ensures no workdays are the same.

Moreover, you will have an important role being an essential part of the rotational 24x7 on-call system, also having the requirement to work overtime, reflecting the continuous nature of data center operations as a Data Center never sleeps. Based on these requirements, it would therefore also be beneficial if you are able to reach our Taastrup site within approx. 45 minutes.

Key Responsibilities and what you will do during a typical week:

• Preventive & Corrective Maintenance: Perform rounds and inspections to conduct preventive and corrective maintenance on critical systems. Inspect and test important equipment such as backup generators, cooling systems, UPS batteries, and electrical panels to ensure optimal performance and early detection of faults.

• Physical Monitoring & Inspections: Carry out daily inspections on infrastructure components to assess technical performance, environmental conditions, and compliance with safety and operational standards.

• Incident & Emergency Response: Monitor and respond rapidly to system alerts, alarms, and emergencies.

• Complex Problem Solving: Troubleshoot and assist with repairing of complex issues across electrical, mechanical, and control systems. Apply systematic problem-solving techniques and escalate when needed.

• Change Management: Support the execution and documentation of system changes, following established Change Management protocols to minimize operational risk.

• Vendor Supervision: Coordinate and supervise external vendors to ensure adherence to operational procedures, safety requirements, and quality standards during maintenance or installation work.

Who we are looking for

You are a dedicated professional with a strong commitment to operational excellence and safety in Mission critical environments. With a blend of technical knowledge and hands-on experience, you are skilled at handling complex systems and processes and thrive in roles where critical infrastructure demands unwavering attention. You are detail-oriented, quick to respond to emergencies, and focused on developing and adhering to robust procedures. Your adaptability and communication skills enable you to work effectively with team members, vendors, and contractors alike.

Why this role matters

Hybrid Greentech is scaling fast as a VPP, BRP and electricity retailer across Denmark, and Northern Europe. Energy trading means large and volatile daily revenue, cost and cash transactions – so quality , accuracy and liquidity control are not back-office topics; they decide how fast we can grow. This role exists to give management, the board and investors numbers they can trust, on time, and to build controls and automation that scale with the business rather than with headcount. The same discipline is needed in our consultancy arm, where technical consultants deliver advisory and EPC management projects: clear project economics, timely invoicing and early warning when a project drifts.

The role

As Financial Controller, you report to our Finance Manager and work closely with the CFO and our accountant in a small, hands-on finance team. You lead the operational and analytical work within the financial steering, reporting and finance and business analytics; running the month-end close, the consolidation of our group entities in Denmark and abroad, balance sheet reconciliations, project controlling and the day-to-day operation of our internal controls. This is an individual contributor role with high ownership and direct visibility towards management.

You will work in close collaboration with our settlement team, project managers and business owners to ensure adequate financial steering and reporting, partner with our accountant on more complex accounting topics, and work across trading, portfolio management, commercial and engineering. We are a tech-first company with high AI adoption, and we expect you to work that way too: AI tools, scripting and automation are your default approach to removing manual work from close, reconciliation and reporting – combined with the judgement to know when a number needs a human review.

**What you will do

**

• Lead and execute the monthly close and group consolidation, including account mapping, intercompany eliminations, reconciliations and variance analysis, and prepare the monthly financial and business review for the CFO, management and the board.

• Set up and run project controlling – project budgets, hours and utilisation, work in progress, milestone and fixed-fee revenue recognition and timely invoicing – giving project managers and business owners clear steering on margin, estimate-to-complete and cash.

• Automate and rebuild our reporting flow – from ERP trial balances to consolidated P&L, balance sheet and cash flow – using AI tools, scripting and data pipelines, replacing manual spreadsheet steps with controlled, repeatable and documented processes.

• Operate and strengthen our internal controls within the framework set by the Finance Manager, including segregation of duties, payment and bank authorisations and documented business procedures, and drive follow-up on auditor recommendations.

• In close collaboration with Settlement, ensure trading-related balances – settlement, imbalance costs, customer prepayments and deposits, and collateral posted to TSOs, DSOs and exchanges – are correctly recognized, invoiced and reconciled

• Support cash and liquidity forecasting and management with the Finance Manager and CFO, including rolling cash forecasts, collateral and trading risk capital tracking, and early warning on cash exposure.

• Prepare and analyse the annual budget and monthly forecast updates for the Finance Manager and CFO, maintaining our driver-based budget model and following up on budget-versus-actual deviations with business owners.

• Handle key accounting areas such as revenue recognition and accruals, capitalisation of development projects, grant periodisation and month-end cost accruals, collaborating with our accountant on more complex accounting topics.

• Support in the year-end close and audit for all group entities, including annual reports, tax specifications and intercompany agreements, in close collaboration with Finance Manager and our external auditors.

• Work closely with our Settlement team and business owners to ensure adequate financial steering and reporting – turning data into insight on gross profit by revenue stream, cost of execution and unit economics, and building dashboards that let the business self-serve.

**

What you bring**

_Experience and skills (Required)

_

• 5+ years of experience as a controller, in audit or in a group finance role, ideally in a multi-entity set-up.

• A relevant degree in accounting, finance or economics (e.g. cand.merc., HD-R or cand.merc.aud.).

• Proven hands-on experience running month-end close, consolidation and year-end audit under the Danish Financial Statements Act (Årsregnskabsloven)

• Hands-on experience with ERP systems, preferably e-conomic

• Solid understanding of balance sheet accounting, revenue recognition, capitalised development costs, accruals and intercompany transactions.

• Experience with project controlling – budgets, work in progress, utilisation and project margin follow-up – ideally in a consultancy, engineering, Trading or EPC business.

• A genuine AI-first way of working: you use AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot daily and can show concrete examples of finance processes you have automated (e.g. with Python, SQL, Power Query, APIs or low-code tools).

• Strong Excel and financial modelling skills combined with a structured, control-minded approach and high attention to detail.

• The ability to work independently in a fast-paced scale-up, prioritise under pressure and explain financial matters clearly to non-finance colleagues.

• Language: English (required); Danish

_Nice to have

_

• Experience from energy trading, utilities, commodities or financial services – e.g. settlement, collateral, imbalance or margin processes.

• Experience with e-conomic, time registration or PSA tools, ERP migration to a more scalable platform, and BI tools such as Power BI.

• Experience with public grant-funded projects, transfer pricing or building internal controls in a growth company.

• A background from a Big 4 or mid-tier audit firm.

**What we offer

• Real responsibility: the chance to improve how close, controls and reporting are run in a scaling energy trading group – not just maintain them.

• An AI-first workplace where you get the tools and the mandate to automate, experiment and rethink how finance is done, working closely with our CFO, trading and tech teams with exposure to board and investor reporting.

• A collaborative environment with short decision lines, high trust, and strong cross-functional execution.

Ready to apply?

Ready to build an AI-first finance function for a company where every megawatt-hour traded must be settled, reconciled and controlled? If you combine accounting rigour with a builder's mindset, we would love to hear from you.

Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis until 10 December. We reserve the right to close this vacancy earlier if a suitable candidate is identified and accepted.
